newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up slightly at the close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up slightly at the close.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices finished Wednesday's session up slightly, outperforming the Treasury market, traders said.

The Treasury market's two point rally from Tuesday ended with a thud Wednesday, as profit taking sparked by disappointing new home sales hit the market. The Treasury long bond was down 8/32 at 100-19/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
The muni futures market also outperformed, with the December contract closing up 7/32 to 115-8/32.
That compared to an unchanged T-bond contract, which held steady at 112-19/32 and widened the MOB spread between the two contracts to 85 ticks from 78 ticks at the close Tuesday.
In the muni secondary, bids on Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2025 were up one basis point, at 5.72 percent, after dropping three basis points earlier in the day.
PaineWebber said it repriced the New York Urban Development Corp's $592 million deal, raising yields in several maturities and lifting the top yield in 2026 to 5.88 percent from 5.86 percent.

Other negotiated offerings included Shelby County, Tenn.'s $107 million general obligation deal. Goldman Sachs & Co repriced the deal, lowering yields in several maturities and cutting the top yield in 2009 to 5.80 percent from 5.85 percent.

Smith Barney Inc won the week's largest competitive deal, a $133 million Virginia Public School Authority issue which apparently moved quickly. Just one hour after the deal was priced, Smith Barney said the account was closed.
In other competitive action, Goldman Sachs & Co won $89.9 million Nassau County, N.Y., unlimited tax bonds, reoffering the deal at a top yield of 5.55 percent in 2015.

The new issue parade continues Thursday, when competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.54 billion in 26 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $137 million in 12 offerings, with a $79 million Mississippi general obligation deal at 1100 EST the largest issue.
Negotiated sales total $1.4 billion in 14 offerings. The largest issue is a $775 million taxable New York State Dormitory Authority deal through Lehman Brothers.
Thursday data releases include personal income and consumption for September at 0830 EST, expected to show 0.6 percent and 0.3 percent increases, respectively.
The Chicago Purchasing Managers Index is forecast at 54.0 for October. That figure is set for release at 1000 EST. --Steven Dickson, 212-859-1652 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
